Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The worst-case cost for a single operation on a vertex $v$ is determined by the maximum number of outgoing edges from any vertex in the graph, which can be as high as $|V| - 1$. Therefore, the upper bound for the worst possible single operation is $O(|V|)$.
* The total cost of the sequence of operations is equal to the sum of the out-degrees of all vertices, which corresponds exactly to the total number of edges in the graph, denoted as $|E|$.
* By applying aggregate analysis, the average amortized cost per operation is calculated by dividing the total cost by the number of operations ($|V|$), resulting in an amortized cost of $O(|E|/|V|)$.
